subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Is the mock Azure Responses probe plus focused resolver coverage enough proof for this auth-provider routing fix, or should live Azure credential proof be required before merge?
rationale: The patch is a narrow resolver fix with good mock/live-output evidence, but it changes provider/auth ownership and repository policy treats external API behavior as needing strong proof when feasible.

options.title: Accept mock routing proof
options.body: Proceed after exact-head CI or focused resolver checks because the proof directly shows OpenClaw routing to the configured Azure Responses URL and API-key header without requiring real Azure credentials.

options.title: Require live Azure proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted live Azure account probe before merge if maintainers want credential-exchange evidence for this auth-provider boundary.

options.title: Pause for owner review
options.body: Keep the PR open without merge until an agents/provider owner decides the proof standard.

recommendation.title: Accept mock routing proof
recommendation.body: Proceed after exact-head CI or focused resolver checks because the proof directly shows OpenClaw routing to the configured Azure Responses URL and API-key header without requiring real Azure credentials.
